title: AMBER: A Unified Accelerator for Multi-Precision LLM Inference Exploiting Bit-Level Redundancy and Reconfigurability
evidence_span: AMBER uses bit-transposed encoding for lossless compression across INT, floating-point, and microscaling formats, plus a precision-agnostic stage-pipelined bit-serial PE that reuses bit-level redundancy; across eight LLMs and ten formats the official description reports 1.17x memory-efficiency and 3.16x compute improvements over Olive and Tender.
problem: LLM deployments use diverse numeric formats while accelerators are usually specialized for only a few precisions, limiting reuse and compression across cloud and edge settings.
method_or_artifact: Bit-transposed lossless weight/KV compression and reconfigurable bit-serial processing elements supporting INT, FP, and MX formats.
workload_or_benchmark: Eight LLMs and ten precision formats across cloud/edge inference; model sizes, accuracy constraints, hardware target, and format mix are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: General-purpose multi-precision accelerator with bit-serial PE pipeline and compressed weight/KV storage; process, memory hierarchy, area, and clock are unspecified.
limits: The description omits model accuracy, compression ratio by format, area/power, memory bandwidth, and baseline configurations.
Lossless compression and bit-serial reuse may trade off decode/control overhead and throughput across formats.
Official description only; accelerator and quality claims require paper-level verification.

title: SAEM: Stage-Aware Expert Management for Memory-Efficient MoE Inference in Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
evidence_span: SAEM detects chain-of-thought reasoning stage boundaries, exploits coherent expert activation for stage-aware GPU/CPU caching, and combines token packing with in-situ CPU execution; the official description reports 1.54x speedup over state-of-the-art baselines under memory constraints.
problem: CoT decoding increases latency and memory use, while MoE expert weights exceed GPU capacity and token-uniform runtimes cause inefficient caching and GPU-CPU movement.
method_or_artifact: Stage-boundary detection, stage-aware expert placement/caching, token packing, and CPU execution integrated into an MoE serving runtime.
workload_or_benchmark: Chain-of-thought MoE inference under constrained GPU memory; model, stage distributions, GPU/CPU capacities, quality metrics, and baselines are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: GPU plus CPU memory and transfer path for expert weights; interconnect, bandwidth, memory capacity, and CPU execution support are unspecified.
limits: The description omits model and CoT trace, memory capacities, transfer cost, cache hit rate, and output-quality conditions.
Stage coherence may vary by prompt and reasoning workload, affecting generality.
Official description only; runtime and quality claims require paper-level verification.

title: Accelerating GPU Inference of Large Language Models with Moderately Unstructured Sparse Weight Matrices
evidence_span: The method combines Sparse-TC storage for sparse tensor cores, Slot-Filling compression with parallel differential-distance decoding, a residual layer for exact sparse matrix multiplication, and a kernel that overlaps CUDA-core computation with memory access; the official description reports up to 1.64x kernel speedup over SpInfer and 1.41x end-to-end speedup over FlashLLM at moderate sparsity, with source code linked.
problem: Moderate unstructured sparsity can preserve LLM quality but existing GPU SpMM kernels fail to beat dense multiplication at roughly 50% sparsity.
method_or_artifact: Three-layer sparse storage format and hybrid sparse-tensor-core/CUDA SpMM kernel with compressed on-chip decoding and residual correction.
workload_or_benchmark: LLM GPU inference with moderately sparse weight matrices and HBM-equipped GPUs; sparsity patterns, models, accuracy, and GPU configurations are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Modern GPU with sparse tensor cores, CUDA cores, and high-bandwidth memory; architecture, kernel launch settings, and precision are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 1.64x kernel-level speedup over SpInfer
Up to 1.41x end-to-end speedup over FlashLLM
limits: The description omits sparsity distribution, model accuracy, GPU models, batch/sequence settings, memory traffic, and baseline tuning.
Kernel-level and end-to-end gains have different boundaries and may vary with sparsity structure.
Official description and linked source require paper-level artifact and correctness verification.
evidence_locators: Linked source repository in official description

title: Attackonctf: Defending Hardware Security Competition Benchmarks in the Age of LLMs
evidence_span: The study finds LLM detectors can exploit diff-style syntax in HackTheSilicon benchmarks, reaching an 83% detection rate without genuine security reasoning; it proposes semantics-preserving, human-readable obfuscation and controlled diff noise, reporting 50% lower detection accuracy with 10% obfuscation and 78.6% reduction under complete obfuscation.
problem: Hardware-security competition benchmarks can be invalidated when LLM detectors exploit superficial syntax rather than vulnerability semantics.
method_or_artifact: LLM-oriented semantics-preserving benchmark obfuscation with human-readable transformations and controlled diff noise.
workload_or_benchmark: HackTheSilicon hardware-security competition benchmark and LLM-based vulnerability detectors; detector models, task distribution, and accuracy definition are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Hardware-security benchmark source code and vulnerability-detection workflow; IP designs, languages, and evaluation environment are unspecified.
metrics: 78.6% lower detection accuracy under complete obfuscation
limits: The description omits detector identities, benchmark size, semantic-equivalence tests, and distinction between accuracy reduction and restored validity.
Obfuscation may alter task difficulty or hide meaningful vulnerability cues despite preserving function.
Official description only; benchmark validity and security conclusions require paper-level verification.

title: PiMM-NoC: Process-in-Memristor-Memory NoC with RL Mapping Framework for Versatile AI Models
evidence_span: PiMM-NoC combines weight-stationary PiMM tiles with processing units for non-weight-stationary and nonlinear operations, then uses a cycle-accurate simulator and Monte Carlo Tree Search within an RL hardware-software co-design framework to map diverse AI workloads; the official description reports 3.45x DNN and 3.85x LLM speedups over existing mapping strategies, plus 71.6x performance and 6.7x energy-efficiency over state-of-the-art accelerators.
problem: Existing process-in-memristor-memory designs support narrow model classes and use coarse static mappings that underexploit the architecture’s design space.
method_or_artifact: Heterogeneous PiMM/PU tile NoC and reinforcement-learning/MCTS mapping search coupled to cycle-accurate architecture simulation.
workload_or_benchmark: Versatile DNN and LLM workloads; model suite, mapping objectives, process/device parameters, and baseline accelerator configurations are unspecified.
hardware_or_process_assumptions: Process-in-memristor-memory tiles with weight-stationary and general processing units connected by a NoC; memristor technology, precision, ADC/DAC, area, and power assumptions are unspecified.
metrics: Up to 71.6x performance over state-of-the-art accelerators
limits: The description omits model and mapping sets, simulator validation, memristor nonidealities, peripheral costs, and baseline normalization.
Large performance ranges may reflect different baselines and workload mappings rather than one common comparison.
Official description only; architecture, device, and energy claims require paper-level verification.
